Cullen Skink Chowder

Served at: St. Andrew's Day

Serves 4Prep 15 minCook 30 min

Cullen Skink is a traditional Scottish smoked haddock soup, rich and creamy, often enjoyed on St. Andrew's Day to celebrate Scotland's patron saint. This hearty chowder combines smoked fish, potatoes, and onions, embodying the rustic flavors of Scottish coastal cuisine.

Ingredients

  • 1 lb (450 g) smoked haddock fillets, skin removed
  • 4 cups (1 L) whole milk
  • 2 cups (480 ml) water
  • 1 large onion, finely chopped
  • 2 cups (300 g) potatoes, peeled and diced
  • 2 tablespoons (30 g) unsalted butter
  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) heavy cream
  • Salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
  • 2 tablespoons (8 g) fresh parsley, chopped

Method

  1. Place the smoked haddock fillets in a large saucepan with the milk and water.
  2. Gently heat the mixture over medium heat until just simmering, then reduce the heat and poach the fish for about 10 minutes until cooked through.
  3. Remove the fish from the liquid and set aside to cool slightly.
  4. Strain the poaching liquid and return it to the saucepan.
  5. In a separate pan, melt the butter and gently sauté the chopped onion until soft and translucent.
  6. Add the diced potatoes to the poaching liquid and bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until the potatoes are tender, about 15 minutes.
  7. Flake the smoked haddock, removing any bones.
  8. Add the sautéed onions and flaked fish to the soup base.
  9. Stir in the heavy cream and heat gently without boiling.
  10. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
  11. Serve hot, garnished with chopped fresh parsley.

Tips

  • Use good-quality smoked haddock for the best flavor; avoid overly salty varieties.
  • For a thicker chowder, mash some of the cooked potatoes before adding the fish.
  • Serve with crusty bread or oatcakes for a traditional Scottish accompaniment.
